stage: Generated original-JSON knee-only leg; preview owns a reversible root translation and stops at first foot contact
algorithm: Deterministic UI, analytic ballistic and quasistatic mesh-readiness evaluation; no ML
observations: World-space foot/floor clearance and physical elapsed time
Incident speed and kinetic energy before contact
UI pause/replay/return, exact local FEM mesh preservation, diagnostic visibility
Mesh PET/PLA volumes and compression at four refinement levels
Accepted and rejected cable loads, numeric patch/equilibrium tests
actions: Choose authorized provisional 50 g mass; 70 mm height specified by user
Run 13 numerical tests (9 FEM implementation, 4 ballistics)
Exercise actual preview, pause/resume, save, return, cable demo and fractional Rebuild rejection buttons
Repeat five actual Apply accepted/rejected-load cases
Refresh workshop while preview active; verify cancellation recovery and live updater
Visually inspect full-app screenshot and remove stale cable-direction glyphs from preview

commands: Return to cable FEM, then send exact_joint/validate_apply_live.py --timeout 45
evaluation.conditions: Baseline 30 mm source joint; PLA 0.4 mm, PET 80 um, assumed 0.2 mm gap and elastic moduli. Upright foot-first release, zero cable tensions, rigid horizontal floor, no payload. Local stage safety export preserved before initial code refresh.
evaluation.known_failure_fixed: An active-preview maintenance refresh exposed CancelledError from a newly created updater cancelled before its first frame. Parent callers now handle cancellation; the final regression includes this case.

limitations: Quasistatic FEM has no mass/inertia or transient impact integration
No foot contact, self-contact, impact damping or restitution model
No calibrated rate-dependent PLA/PET failure or adhesive separation law
Mesh response is unconverged; PET reference volume changes with refinement
Measured mass distribution, material coupons and impact data are unavailable
notes: No dynamic impact FEM, fracture calculation or survival verdict. Passing functional tests does not validate stresses. Earlier v8/v9 and FEA/ML artifacts preserved. Mass and landing orientation/surface are labelled assumptions, not measured Sony test replication.
